title: Daily Temperatures
statement: For each day, return how many days you must wait for a strictly warmer temperature, or 0 if no warmer day follows.

hints.1_question: For each day you want the next day that is warmer. Which earlier days are still 'waiting' when you see a new temperature?
hints.2_nudge: Keep a stack of indices of days still waiting for a warmer day. A new temperature resolves every waiting day that is colder than it.
hints.3_big_hint: For each i: while stack and temps[stack[-1]] < temps[i]: j = pop; ans[j] = i - j. Then push i. Leftover days stay 0.

known_bugs.name: pops on equal temperatures too (<=)
known_bugs.followup: The problem wants a strictly warmer day. Is an equal temperature warmer?

known_bugs.name: only looks at tomorrow
known_bugs.followup: What if the warmer day is three days away rather than tomorrow?

known_bugs.name: nested scan from every day (O(n^2))
known_bugs.followup: On a list that only gets colder, how many comparisons does your scan make? Can you reuse earlier work?

followups: Each index is pushed and popped at most once. Why does that make it O(n)?
How would you find the previous warmer day instead?
